title: CLI zero-config repro labs and traffic synthesis (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a minimal, zero-configuration CLI lab that lets a developer reproduce local SDK/CLI issues, run synthetic traffic to exercise edge cases (rate limits, token batching, streaming cutovers), and capture lightweight telemetry that aligns with our Console metrics. The aim is a 5–10 minute local run that surfaces common failure modes and provides deterministic inputs for bug reports and quick PR validation.

Audience:
- Developer experience engineers onboarding SDK regressions
- Solutions engineers reproducing customer edge cases
- QA and reliability engineers validating fixes before a Dedicated rollout

Quick goals (MVP):
- One executable script: run-lab.sh (or run-lab.ps1) that works with zero creds (uses dev token stub)
- Scenario matrix: smoke, burst-rate-limit, long-stream, kvcache-regress, quantized-path-fallthrough
- Output: unified lab.log + minimal JSON telemetry compatible with Console ingestion fields (route, model_variant, latency_ms, tokens_out, error_code)
- Auto-attach artifacts: reproducible prompt set, seed values, captured stdout/stderr, cURL snippets

High-level flow (developer):
1) git clone github.com/redwood-inference/cli-proto && cd cli-proto
2) ./run-lab.sh --scenario burst --duration 30s --seed 1234
3) open artifacts/last-run/ for lab.log + telemetry.json + repro-requests.txt
4) paste telemetry.json + repro-requests.txt into a bug report template

Core components in repo (sketch):
- run-lab.sh: orchestrates scenarios, sets environment variables for zero-config mode, collects artifacts
- scenarios/: JS/Python scripts that send requests to local runner or to a mocked hosted endpoint
- mock_server/: minimal express/fastapi server that can simulate rate limits, partial stream chunking, 429/503 responses, and slow KV cache hits
- telemetry-normalizer.py: emits flattened telemetry lines that map to Console schema (CSV/JSONL)
- generators/: prompt_set_generator and traffic_synth that build deterministic streams from a seed

Example CLI usage (zero config):
- ./run-lab.sh --scenario smoke
- ./run-lab.sh --scenario burst --qps 50 --duration 60 --capture-websocket
- ./run-lab.sh --scenario streaming-fade --model variant-a --seed 2025

Scenario descriptions (initial set):
- smoke: single short prompt, validates happy path and token accounting
- burst: small prompt repeated at increasing QPS to trigger batching and queue/backpressure; records queue length and latency percentiles
- streaming-fade: long-stream responses truncated mid-message (simulate client disconnect) and server fallback to polling path
- kvcache-drift: repeated prompt with small prefix differences to exercise prefix cache misses and KV eviction heuristics
- quant-fallback: request a quantized model variant then force fallback to FP32 path to validate correct logging of model_variant fallthroughs

Telemetry fields to capture (minimal normalized set):
route, model_variant, scenario, run_id, request_id, timestamp, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, status, error_code, qps_target, observed_qps, queue_depth, client_disconnect_flag
(keep values as strings/numbers in telemetry.json but for the lab deliverable we provide the flattened JSONL file)

Artifact structure after run (example):
artifacts/last-run/
  lab.log                      -- full stdout+stderr, raw
  telemetry.jsonl              -- newline-delimited normalized telemetry
  repro-requests.txt           -- exact requests sent (with seed)
  mock-server-traces.txt       -- if mock server used
  scenario-config.yaml         -- parameters used for run
  local-dump.tar.gz            -- optional full capture for heavy debugging

Quickstart for triage (template for a solutions engineer):
1) run burst scenario with seed from customer report: ./run-lab.sh --scenario burst --seed 8423 --duration 45
2) open telemetry.jsonl and check for 5xx/429 spikes around same seed timestamps
3) if queue_depth > 5 and latency p95 > 500ms, attach lab.log + repro-requests.txt to JIRA issue and add label `repro/cli-burst`
4) if streaming-fade observed, include mock-server-traces.txt and mark for runtime team (serving-runtime)

Mini checklists (for each run):
- [ ] Scenario and seed documented in scenario-config.yaml
- [ ] Lab captured telemetry.jsonl and lab.log produced
- [ ] Repro requests attached and shortened to minimal failing set
- [ ] Linked PR / branch noted in lab header

Open questions / TODOs (short-term):
- Do we standardize field names to match Console exactly (route vs api_route)? My preference: map to Console aliases but include both in telemetry.jsonl for backward compat.
- Should run-lab default to a small local dockerized runtime or use an in-process mock server? Docker has higher fidelity but adds friction. Proposal: default mock server, opt-in --use-docker for more realistic path.
- Auth: zero-config mode uses a synthetic token; need to document how to switch to real tokens for sensitive repros.

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- run-lab.sh runs on macOS/Linux with no external deps beyond python3/node installed
- A reproducible failing sequence can be captured and replayed by another engineer using the seed and artifacts in under 10 minutes
- Telemetry JSONL maps to Console schema for at least 90% of fields used in rolling dashboards (route, model_variant, latency, tokens_out, error_code)

Notes for implementation team (practical heuristics):
- Keep scenarios focused: start with 5 deterministic flows rather than a big combinatorial grid
- Use a single seed-driven prompt generator so that requests are compact and stable across runs
- Make mock-server behavior deterministic: seeded random delays and a fixed pattern for 429/503 responses, with option to read a fault-script (for advanced repros)
- Build minimal adapter so that telemetry.jsonl can be dropped into Console ingestion for local visualization (simple CSV -> Console import)

Example minimal mock-server snippet (pseudo):
- route /v1/generate returns streaming chunks every 30-120ms; if random(seed) < 0.08 then insert partial chunk and close socket (simulate client disconnect)
- rate limiter increments counter per second and returns 429 after threshold reached; logs bucket and backpressure metrics

Communication checklist when filing a customer-facing repro:
- include exact run command used and the seed value
- attach telemetry.jsonl (first 100 lines) and repro-requests.txt (minimized)
- indicate whether mock_server or real runtime was used
- link to branch/PR with run-lab.sh used to generate artifacts

Longer-term ideas (nice-to-have):
- Web UI that replays telemetry.jsonl visually (latency timeline, queue depth heatmap)
- Integrations: one-click attach into a Jira issue with artifacts uploaded to our internal bucket
- Library of curated repros from production incidents, searchable by symptom (e.g., "stream hang", "token double-count")

Misc notes / brain dump (raw):
- Consider adding a tiny CI job that runs the smoke scenario on PRs touching CLI or telemetry code paths
- Might be useful to add a "fuzz" mode that introduces small prompt mutations to test our caching boundaries
- Keep the default prompt set short (3–8 examples) to keep runs light and logs digestible

End of draft.

-- aisha
(reach: #eng-developer-experience Slack, DM preferred for quick sync)
